en.title: Minimum One-Direction Transport Cost to Balance a Ring of Warehouses
en.description:
n warehouses form a ring, and moving one item across an adjacent edge costs 1. The goal is for every warehouse to end up with the same number of items; the total is guaranteed to be divisible by n. The whole plan must use only one direction, either clockwise or counterclockwise, and cannot mix directions; you may choose any starting point. Find the minimum total cost.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains warehouses. The original statement gives no value bounds; on this site 1≤n≤200000, 0≤warehouses[i]≤10^9, and sum%n=0 is guaranteed. Output the exact integer cost, without any modulus.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 8, 7 and 0 respectively. In the first example, moving items in both directions could cost 4, but the original rule of a single direction throughout makes the minimum 8.
hints: Compute the prefix surplus P of each warehouse relative to the average, including the final 0. The minimum cost in the forward direction is sum(P)−n·min(P), and in the reverse direction n·max(P)−sum(P); take the smaller one.
